knowledge:
- key_parameters: BSgenomeName=The BSgenome object representing the target genome used to build the RE map ;; partitionMultipleRE=The strategy used to partition reads mapping to multiple RE sites (options: "unique", "best", "random", "average", "estimate") ;; cut.offset=The offset of the cut site relative to the start of the RE recognition pattern ;; allowed.offset=The allowed offset to guard against imperfect sticky end repair and primer addition ;; min.FragmentLength/max.FragmentLength=The expected range of fragment lengths for assigning reads ;; by=The summarization metric used in summarizeByRE (e.g., "Weight")
- alternatives: For experiments with biological replicates (at least two conditions), count tables generated by summarizeByRE should be analyzed using DESeq or edgeR instead of the built-in compareREDseq function. Differentially cut RE sites can be annotated to the nearest gene using ChIPpeakAnno.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing high-throughput sequencing data from restriction enzyme digestion (REDseq) to identify genome-wide accessible/inaccessible regions or to compare RE digestion profiles across different conditions, cell types, or developmental stages.
- pitfalls: For paired-end sequencing data, assignSeq2REsite cannot be run directly on the paired-end object. Users must first extract the start and end coordinates into separate GRanges objects (e.g., using start() and end()), call assignSeq2REsite twice (once for each), and set min.FragmentLength = 0, max.FragmentLength = 1, and seq.length = 1 for both calls.

workflows.name: single_end_redseq_analysis
workflows.intent: Build a restriction enzyme map, assign single-end sequence tags to RE sites, visualize distributions, and perform statistical testing for enriched/depleted or differential cut sites.
input: examplePattern.fa (FASTA file containing the restriction enzyme recognition site)
example.REDseq (GRanges object of mapped single-end sequence tags)
example.map (GRanges object of restriction enzyme cut sites)
workflows.stages: 1. Build genome-wide RE map using buildREmap ;; 2. Assign mapped sequence tags to RE sites using assignSeq2REsite ;; 3. Visualize cut frequency distribution using plotCutDistribution and distance distribution using distanceHistSeq2RE ;; 4. Summarize assigned reads to generate a count table using summarizeByRE ;; 5. Identify statistically significant cut sites for a single condition using binom.test.REDseq, or compare two conditions without replicates using compareREDseq
workflows.code:
library(REDseq)
REpatternFilePath = system.file("extdata", "examplePattern.fa", package="REDseq")
library(BSgenome.Celegans.UCSC.ce2)
myMap = buildREmap( REpatternFilePath, BSgenomeName=Celegans, outfile="example.REmap")
data(example.REDseq)
data(example.map)
r.unique = assignSeq2REsite(example.REDseq, example.map, cut.offset = 1, 
seq.length = 36, allowed.offset = 5, min.FragmentLength = 60, 
max.FragmentLength = 300, partitionMultipleRE = "unique")
r.best= assignSeq2REsite(example.REDseq, example.map, 
cut.offset = 1, seq.length = 36, allowed.offset = 5, 
min.FragmentLength = 60, max.FragmentLength = 300, partitionMultipleRE = "best")
r.random = assignSeq2REsite(example.REDseq, example.map, cut.offset = 1, 
seq.length = 36, allowed.offset = 5, min.FragmentLength = 60, 
max.FragmentLength = 300, partitionMultipleRE = "random")
r.average = assignSeq2REsite(example.REDseq, example.map, cut.offset = 1, 
seq.length = 36, allowed.offset = 5, min.FragmentLength = 60,
 max.FragmentLength = 300, partitionMultipleRE = "average")
r.estimate = assignSeq2REsite(example.REDseq, example.map, cut.offset = 1, 
seq.length = 36, allowed.offset = 5, min.FragmentLength = 60, 
max.FragmentLength = 300, partitionMultipleRE = "estimate")
head(r.estimate$passed.filter)
data(example.assignedREDseq)
plotCutDistribution(example.assignedREDseq,example.map, chr="2",
xlim =c(3012000, 3020000))
distanceHistSeq2RE(example.assignedREDseq,ylim=c(0,25))
REsummary  =summarizeByRE(example.assignedREDseq,by="Weight")
binom.test.REDseq(REsummary)
x= cbind(c("RE1", "RE2", "RE3", "RE4"), c(10,1,100, 0),c(5,5,50, 40))
colnames(x) = c("REid", "control", "treated")
compareREDseq(x)
